Replay

Replay implementation and test scope

Implemented contracts, tested configurations, and remaining support limits.

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Requirement-to-evidence tableObserver-effect classificationConcrete closure workCurrent verificationExplicit nonclaims

This audits the eight framework completion gates. It reuses existing integration evidence and runs focused current checks. The final assessment closes the revised framework-first scope; it does not require every game to become a complete remake or claim unverified public/platform support.

Requirement-to-evidence table#

Gate Implementation inspected Evidence and assessment
Complete simulation/replay state replay/timeline.odin, correction.odin, pool.odin, random.odin, value.odin Current core tests cover transactional history, lifetime, RNG, rejected references and failed suffix replay. Implemented for bounded owned values, including tagged unions; dynamic reference graphs are outside the current storage contract.
Godot authoring/presentation godot/session.odin, nodes.odin, input clocks/buttons, view/events.odin, cues and diagnostics Current view/diagnostic tests plus M2 technical evidence cover input edges, pause, view lifetime, reconciliation and detached presentation. Paid revive is an existing cross-entity authoring comparison. Implementation present; consolidated onboarding and checked lifecycle recipes now exist. Human productivity/play-feel superiority is unproven.
Server, co-op and competitive policies net/types.odin, groups.odin, replication policy, owned, Body2/Body3 adapters Current network/interest/owned suites exercise correction, authored footprints, hidden-state projection, ownership scope and reliable action context. This is explicit cooperative ownership coordinated by an authority, not arbitrary simultaneous writers or deterministic Godot physics. Representative game integrations already exist.
Deterministic P2P p2p/runner.odin, archives, spectator/watch/rebind and provisioning Current units and complete default/optimized native/WASM archive, rejoin and spectator-failover corpora pass. The audit exposed an arm64 compiler miscompile in an inlined test-model factory; a fixture-only no-inline workaround and callback-owner assertions preserve the original acceptance checks. Runner semantics are unchanged.
Reusable setup and identity Party/Room, durable enrollment, registration, P2P party/pair service and native links Native P2P and browser receipts cover persisted create/join/rejoin, current incarnations, authenticated connection generations and returned endpoints. The two-peer native owner now separates bind and advertised endpoints, with a real forwarded-port recovery gate.
Session recovery Authority records/leases, complete checkpoints, bounded transfer, Room transitions/publication/restore Current authority/recovery suites plus browser failure matrix, transition expiry, dedicated and recent native/browser migration evidence establish the documented local envelopes. Cold restore and pending-command classification are implemented. Arbitrary partitions/outages and live Steam are not universally validated.
Transport/resource stabilization Common Transport/Router, ENet/RTC, generation fences, canonical codecs, budgets and profiling Current schema/network tests cover malformed inputs, channel/packet limits, transactional decode, baseline recovery and bounded work. Existing native/browser/TURN evidence is scoped. Cavecrawl comparison records higher Replay costs; later compression results address measured traffic overhead only. The consolidated supported-envelope/release assessment records these tradeoffs.
Delivery and compatibility Package docs, runnable examples, versioned schemas/content, explicit checkpoint converters Obsolete capability/version claims were corrected. Consolidated onboarding, compatibility policy, native/WASM checked API recipes and a bounded framework smoke command now exist. The supported-envelope/release assessment and isolated addon gate complete the delivery assessment.

The source paths above refer to current implementation, not planned package names. There is no missing replay/session package to scaffold: its responsibilities are implemented by net, authority, provision, recovery and the Godot owners.

Observer-effect classification#

The current four-process fault/refresh scenario reaches tick 2400 with all 21 authoritative kicks presented. It requests a same-epoch checkpoint while the tick-220 effect is confirmed (222) but not yet visible (watched 214); that effect is emitted exactly once after refresh. Native and standalone WASM consume the same 5,669-frame / 28,085-operation trace and reject corruption.

This verifies the current retained-effect/rebase contract. The older C2 case that lost four effects has no failing delivery trace; its cause remains unestablished. The prior investigation already failed to reproduce it in seven captured schedules. Treat it as a historical, unreproduced report rather than indefinitely rerunning full games or declaring an invented fix. A new failing trace reopens a concrete shared defect.

Concrete closure work#

No implementation item remains in the framework-first closure queue. The support envelope and release assessment classify the modes, limits, comparisons, distribution and P2P control-loss behavior.

No new game-content or visual parity task is implied by this list.

Endpoint separation and setup/compatibility delivery are now verified in the delivery increment.

Current verification#

The audit ran 30 core, 24 view, 182 network, 7 interest, 11 owner-stream, 36 authority, 11 recovery, 33 P2P and 28 schema unit tests: 362 tests. Their scripts also run package-specific WASM/recording checks. The diagnostic script exercises actual checkpoint upgrades and field inspection. The focused observer trace runs separately. This is a framework audit selection, not a claim that the entire repository suite ran.

The initial P2P command failed in optimized native execution. Correct LLVM IR stored the model callback, but final arm64 instructions overwrote its register with an endpoint address before storing Model.step. The no-inline fixture factory avoids that code shape. Split assignments and no-inline runner init did not fix it; none of those experiments changed shipping runtime sources. The final P2P command passes with its direct model() calls and all original world/hash checks. See receipts and assembly excerpt.

Explicit nonclaims#

Managed variable-size simulation collections, multiple independent prediction timelines per client, static schema code generation, and exactly-once external service outboxes are not implemented. The current library uses bounded value storage, one authored prediction group and runtime-compiled canonical codecs. Those are documented design/support boundaries, not hidden fallback behavior. External persistent effects remain outside speculative simulation; frame migration must not be advertised as an exactly-once payment/achievement ledger.

These boundaries do not remove a promised multiplayer style: server authority, cooperative owner streams, competitive prediction and deterministic rollback each have explicit implementations. Additional platforms/backends and public security claims require their own evidence. Original games and all separate ports remain.
